case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 6.5.2010 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for leave to appeal No.1359 of 2009).
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This application for review arises out of the judgment and order 6.5.2010 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1359 of 2009 rejecting the same and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.  59 of 1994 decreeing the suit.

2. The facts leading to the filing of this petition for leave to appeal, in short, are:

<u>3. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 and Money Suit No. 2 of 2002 both in the Court of the Subordinate Judge (Joint District Judge) Second Court, Dhaka. Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 was for declaration of title to the suit land and for a further declaration that the plaintiffs were not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 by the Subordinate Judge, third Court, Dhaka and also for declaration that the kabala executed through Court on 27.02.1980 in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka was fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The suit land measuring an area of 0568 ajutangsha, originally belonging to Khiroda Shundari Daishya, was put to auction for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 660  of 1952-53 and was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and the sale certificate was issued in favour of said Ali Ahmed on 19.11.1953. Possession of the auction purchased land was delivered on 20.01.1954 through Court. Ali Ahmed being in possession of the auction purchased land for more than 12 years got his name mutated in the government record and paid rents accordingly. S.A. Khatian No. 197 and R.S. Khatian No. 1248 were accordingly prepared in his name. He died intestate on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, namely, Khatibunnessa, who inherited the entire suit property as sharer of 4 annas share as his wife and the remaining 12 annas share as per the Doctrine of Return. While owning and possessing the suit property, Khatibunnessa died on 10.02.1978 leaving behind her only full brother Abdul Mannan, who inherited her entire property including the suit property and by a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 29.11.1979, he transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs. Thus the plaintiffs being the 16 annas owners of the suit property were in peaceful possession i thereof. Defendants created forged papers and tried to take possession of the suit property forcibly but owing to the intervention of respectable people of the locality, they failed in their illegal attempt. On 06.07.1980, the defendants along with a process server of the Court and police tried to take over the possession of suit land but the plaintiffs by showing decree of the court resisted them. After making inquiry from the bailiff of the Court the plaintiffs father, Abdul Majid, came to know that the defendants obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, and that the defendants entered into an agreement with one Rasheda Begum for purchase of the suit property on the basis of the said fraudulent decree. Rasheda Begum acquired no title to, and possession in, the suit property and therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title to the suit property on the basis of the bainapatra. The defendants got a kabala executed and registered in their names through Court in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979. Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979. Therefore, the decree passed therein was not binding upon them the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction, which was decreed on 28.03.1984 on contest. Against by the said decree, the defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 before the District Judge, Dhaka, which, on transfer, was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. Feeling aggrieved the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before the High Court Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.05.1992 and against which the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.  297 of 1972 before the Appellate Division, and the same was dismissed.</u>

4. On 27.10.1993, the plaintiffs filed an application under order 21 Rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980, arising out of the  decree passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979, and the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 29.01,1994 rejected the application. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property through the said execution case, they were telling the people of the locality that they would soon dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property. The cause of action for the suit arose on 21.10.1993 when the defendants along with the bailiff of the Court asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them and the same was continuing in view of the claim of the defendants. While the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing, the defendants along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.1997 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom. They looted away the household articles worth Tk.6,00,000/-, and also looted away the goods from 10(ten) family rooms and 13 (thirteen) shops in the suit property and took possession thereof. The defendants deprived the plaintiffs of getting rent from the tenants of the said family rooms and shops to the tune of taka 26,000/- per month. After the incident Mr. Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs, lodged an First Information Report (FIR) with Lalbagh Police Station under Section 144/447/44 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants one Wazir Ahmed also lodged an FIR with the said police station which was registered as Lalbagh P.S. Case No. 940 dated 16/09/1997. Subsequently the defendants by putting threat on the life of the plaintiffs as well as their father Abdul Majid and also by applying force got a white paper signed from them with the writing to the effect ‘‘১৬,৬০,০০০/- টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম" though they received no money from the defendants. The defendants demolished the one storied building and the shop rooms standing on the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. From the semi pucca family quarter and the 13 (thirteen) shops the plaintiffs were earning Tk. 26,000/-per month; so they are entitled to get mesne profit at the said rate from that date. In the premises the plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 2 of 2002 claiming Tk.28,71,900/- with interest And cost.

<u>5. The petitioners herein contested the suits by filing written statements. Their case, in short, is that the suit property known as No.  1 Atash Khana Lane, along with other property owned by Khiroda Shundari Daishaya by purchase from (i)Binodini Daishaya by a registered kabala being No. 2892 of 1899 (ii) Shayam Chandra Shaha by a registered kabala being No. 3070 of 1899 and from Rai Mohan Shaha vide kabala No. 3430. Khiroda Sundari Daishaya purchased a portion of C.S. Plot No. 40 of C.S. Khatian No. 237 from Radha Ballav Shaha by a registered kabala dated 04/03/1932 and thus she remained in possession thereof as  the rightful owner. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa by a registered kabala dated 27/03/1953 and delivered possession thereof to her. While in possession of the suit property by paying rents, Salimunnesa transferred her 8(eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8(eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15/06/1959 who later by a registered deed of gift transferred his said 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession thereof to her. Thus Rasheda Begum became the 16 (sixteen) annas owner and possessor of the suit property. One Munjurul Hoq was a tenant in a portion of the suit property and as he defaulted in paying rent Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the Court of the then Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka for the realization of arrear rents. In the same court Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for eviction of said tenant, Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed, and that the tenant forging signature of Rasheda Begum filed two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively in the said money suit and the house rent case and obtained compromise decrees. When Rasheda Begum came to know about the same, she filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deed of agreement dated 16/11/1959 as well as the applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959. Rasheda Begum claimed that the owners of No. 1 Atash Khaha Jane, the suit property, were Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash, who sold the said property to Salimunnesa on 27/05/1954. Defendant No. 2, Khatimunnesa of the said suit was the wife of Doctor Munjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed, a tenant under Khiroda Sundari Daisyha and Lalit Mohan Dash and thus after the transfer of the suit property she became a tenant under Salimunnesa. Thereafter Salimunnesa sold her eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8 (eight) annas share to Md. Bias along with the tenancy right of Khatimunnesa, and as she defaulted in paying the house rent, Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rent and Md. Bias filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for eviction of Khatimunnesa. Monjurul Hoque filed false complaints before the Anti-Corruption Department and the Martial Law News-Centre. Rasheda Begum was a pardanishin lady. At the ill advice of Manjurul Haque, the then-in-charge of Martial Law News Centre, Major Sharif, obtained the signatures of Rasheda Begum on two agreements and the compromise applications by coercion without disclosing the contents thereof. As the said agreements and the applications for compromise were created against the will of Rasheda Begum, she filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964, in which Khatimunnesa and Doctor Manjurul Haque appeared and filed written statement claiming that they purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit holding in auction on 20.06.1953. Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum declaring that the registered agreements being Nos. 6904 and 6905 dated 16.11.1959 were void and ineffective and that the two compromise applications filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 were void. Against the judgment and decree Doctor Manjurul Haque and his wife Khatimunnesa filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka, which on transfer was headed by a Subordinate Judge, who dismissed the said appeal by his judgment and decree dated 19.07.1966 affirming those of the trial Court. Doctor Manjurul Haque and his wife filed Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 before the then High Court and the appeal was also dismissed. Thus the right, title and possession of Rasheda Begum in the suit property was confirmed. While in possession of the suit property, Rasheda Begum entered into a contract with the defendants to sell the same at a price of Tk. 45,000/- and on receipt of a sum of Tk.15,000- as advance executed a bainapatra on 12.08.1972. As Rasheda Begum was avoiding execution and registration of the required kabala, the defendants filed Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The slat was decreed on 15.11.1979 and the defendants got the kabala executed and registered on 27.02.1980 through Court in Title Execution Case No. 03 of 1980. After the registration of the kabala when the defendants went to take possession of the suit property through Court, the plaintiffs resisted and the bailiff of the Court returned the 'writ of delivery' without executing the same with the prayer for police help. Meanwhile, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for permanent   injunction and obtained a decree; which was sot aside by the Appellate Court on 24.01.1987 in Title Appeal No. 1969 of 1984 filed by the defendants. The decree of the Appellate Court was upheld in Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 by the High Court Division discharging the Rule as well as in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 297 of 1992 by the Appellate Division dismissing the petition. After disposal of the said Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, the defendants prayed for police help to execute the decree and the Court allowed the prayer. The plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure just to block the further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. The application was rejected on 23.01.1994 on contest. After that, the plaintiffs filed the instant suit making false and frivolous allegations just to continue with their illegal possession in the suit property depriving the defendants of the enjoyment of the fruits of the aforesaid decree. They further denied the claim of the plaintiffs that they were dispossessed by them by force from the suit property on 16.09.1997 and also denied the fact of looting away the goods from the suit property including from the tenanted rooms and shops causing financial loss of Tk. 20,00,000/- (twenty lacs) and the facts of getting rents from the tenants to the tune of Tk. 26,000/- per month. When Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 was revived the plaintiffs filed an application for staying further proceedings of the same but their prayer was rejected on 29.01.1994. Against the said order, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 465 of 1994 before the High Court Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.08.1997 with a direction upon them to hand over the possession of the suit property to the defendants within 30(thirty) days. After getting possession of the suit land and the other adjacent lands, the defendants demolished the kucha and semi pucca rooms standing thereon. By investing lacs of taka they completed major portion of works for construction of a multistoried building and the remaining work was also under process. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 hereof filed Money Suit No. 73 of 2000 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for realisation of compensation of Tk.28,71,900/-(Twenty Eight lacs Seventy One Thousand and Nine Hundred) along with interest of Tk.15% till realisation and the said suit was transferred to the Subordinate judge (Joint District Judge)  Second Court and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 2 of 2002.</u>

6. These petitioners contested the said money suit by filing written statement denying the claim.

7. Both the title suit and the money suit were heard analogously.

8. The learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka, vide his judgment and decree dated 21.03.2004 decreed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 and the Money Suit No. 2 of 2002. Against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994, these petitioners filed First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 and against the judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No. 2 of 2002 these petitioners filed First Appeal No. 180 of 2004 in the High Court Division and the learned Judges of the High Court Division vide judgments and decrees dated 13.05.2008 dismissed both the First Appeals. Hence these petitions.

9. Against the judgment and decree passed in First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 defendants moved this Court by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 135 of 2009 and by the impugned judgment and order, this Court dismissed the leave petition on 6.5.2010.

10. After that, the defendants preferred this petition for review.

11. Perused the petition seeking review and the impugned judgment and order and other papers on record.

12. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel for the review petitioner, submits that by the Gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 Memo 4024 L.R and LR 4836 LR respectively under section 3 of State Acquisition as amended by E.B. Ordinance 111 of 1956, the rent receiving interest vested in the government on 02.04.1956 and exhibit-1 shows Khiroda Sundari held a Mrish Ijara interest under a private landlord and it conclusively proves that the Certificate Case Number 660 of 1952-53 issued by L.R. government acquired estate is a manufactured paper and exhibits-2 and 2(Ka) are also forged papers and the claim of title of the plaintiffs falls through.

13. The learned Counsel further submits that the finding that the certificate case was filed by the Government for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 while exhibits 2 and 2(Ka) show that certificate case was filed by R.L Government Acquired Estate against the provision of Section 4 of Public Demand Recovery Act is a mistake apparent on the face of record and in the circumstances judgment dated 06.05.2010 calls for review.

14. Mr. M.I. Faroqui, learned counsel for the respondent, submits that the petitioners miserably failed to make out any case for review of the impugned judgment.

15. The above submissions made on behalf of the petitioners merit consideration.

<u>16. Leave is granted to consider the following points:</u>

<u>I. Whether the Gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 Memo 4024 LE and LR 4836 LR respectively under section 3 of State Acquisition as amended by E.B. Ordinance 111 of 1956, the rent receiving interest vested in the government on 02.04.1956 and exhibit-1 shows Khiroda Sundari held a Mrish Ijara interest under a private land lord and it conclusively proves that the certificate case Number 660 of 1952-53 issued by L.R. government acquired estate is a manufactured papers and exhibits-2 and 2(Ka) are all also forged papers and the claim of title of the plaintiff falls through.</u>

<u>II. Whether the finding that the certificate was filed by the Government for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 while the exhibits; 2 and 2(1(a) show that certificate was  filed by R.L Government Acquired Estate against the provision of Section 4 of Public Demand Recovery Act is a mistake apparent on the face of record and in the circumstances, judgment dated 06.05.2010 calls for review.</u>

17. The petitioner is permitted to prepare the paper book out of Court in accordance with the Rules.

18. Further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 09 of 2010 and Money Execution  Case No. 03 of 2010 of the court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka both arising out of Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 be stayed till disposal of the appeal.

End.
